nameStory: The Elongate Stilt Spider gets its name from its remarkably stretched-out body shape and extremely long, thin legs that look like walking stilts. Like a circus performer on stilts, this spider appears to balance delicately on its thread-like legs, giving it an almost comical, stretched appearance that makes it instantly recognizable among the long-jawed orbweavers.
description: The Elongate Stilt Spider is a slender, delicate-looking spider with an unusually long, narrow body and incredibly thin legs that seem almost too fragile to support it. This small orbweaver typically measures less than half an inch in body length, but its legs can span much wider, giving it a distinctive stretched appearance. It belongs to the long-jawed orbweaver family, known for their elongated jaws and tendency to build horizontal or slanted webs near water. Despite its delicate appearance, this spider is a capable predator of small flying insects.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Extremely elongated, narrow body that looks stretched like taffy, with a length much greater than width, giving it an almost stick-like silhouette

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Small body under half an inch long, but appears larger due to very long, thread-thin legs that feel incredibly delicate if touched

idTips.label: Web
idTips.description: Builds horizontal or slightly inclined orb webs, often with an open center, positioned close to water or damp areas

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: Often stretches its body and front legs in a straight line along grass stems or twigs when threatened, becoming nearly invisible

idTips.label: Eyes
idTips.description: Eight eyes arranged in two rows, with the characteristic long jaws (chelicerae) extending forward from the front of the head

habitat: Found in wetland edges, near ponds, streams, and marshes throughout New England, where they prefer areas with tall grasses and reedy vegetation. They favor spots with high humidity close to water sources, often building their webs among cattails, sedges, and other moisture-loving plants. Look for them in the transitional zones between open water and dry land, especially in areas with gentle slopes and soft, organic soils.

seasonality.spring: Adults begin appearing in late spring as temperatures warm, starting to build their first webs in emerging wetland vegetation.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when adults are most visible, actively hunting and mating, with webs most easily spotted in morning dew.
seasonality.fall: Egg sacs are produced and adults remain active until first hard frosts, though they become less conspicuous as vegetation dies back.
seasonality.winter: Adults typically die off with hard frosts, while eggs overwinter in protected locations to emerge the following spring.

funFact: When threatened, the Elongate Stilt Spider can make itself completely invisible by stretching its front legs straight forward and aligning its body perfectly along a grass blade or twig, transforming from a recognizable spider into what looks like just another piece of plant stem.
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with other stretch spiders in the same genus, but the Elongate Stilt Spider has the most extremely stretched body proportions of all. Remember: if it looks almost impossibly thin and stretched, like someone pulled a normal spider through a pasta machine, it's likely the Elongate Stilt Spider.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called 'long-jawed orbweavers,' these spiders' 'long jaws' are actually their chelicerae (the pincer-like mouthparts), not true jaws like mammals have. The term is a common name that stuck, but it refers to these prominent forward-projecting feeding structures that help them handle prey.
compareHints: Among its stretch spider relatives, the Elongate Stilt Spider has the most extreme body elongation - much more stretched than the Common Stretch Spider or Green Long-jawed Orbweaver. While the Silver Long-jawed Orbweaver might be similar in size, it has a more typical spider body proportion and distinctive silvery coloration, whereas the Elongate Stilt Spider's defining feature is its almost absurdly stretched, stick-like body shape.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Among its Tetragnatha relatives, the Green Long-jawed Orbweaver stands out with its vivid green coloration, while the Common Stretch Spider tends to be more yellowish or brownish, and the Silver Long-jawed Orbweaver has distinctive metallic silver markings.
Among New England's long-jawed orbweavers, the Common Stretch Spider is distinguished by its extreme elongation and distinctive straight-line defensive posture.
